question: to the Commission Arkadiusz Mularczyk (ECR) Subject:

The Foundation Remembrance, Responsibility and Future (EVZ), established in 2000 with contributions from the German Government and German industry, paid approximately EUR 4.4 billion to 1.66 million former forced labourers. However, the payment scheme applied a tiered structure under which forced labourers from Eastern European countries, including Poland, received substantially lower payments than those from Western European countries – despite suffering the same category of crime. EU institutions monitor the EVZ Foundation and its operations1. 1.

Was the Commission involved in any capacity in the design or approval of the EVZ Foundation’s payment structure, and if so, did it raise concerns about the differential payment rates applied to Eastern European, and specifically Polish, forced labourers?

Does the Commission consider that the differential payment structure applied to Polish forced labourers under the EVZ scheme – which resulted in lower compensation for victims from Eastern Europe – was consistent with the principle of equal treatment?
https://www.eurofound.europa.eu/en/publications/all/forced-labour-compensation-scheme-facesdifficulties. 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.9.2026) Within the scope of its competences, the Commission remains committed in assisting Member States to ensure that victims of crime receive fair and adequate compensation. However, EU law does not confer on the Commission a role in supervising or approving the design of arrangements that include compensation, such as the Foundation Remembrance, Responsibility and Future (EVZ). Under EU law, the 2004 Compensation Directive1 obliges Member States to ensure that their national rules provide for the existence of a scheme on compensation to victims of violent intentional crimes committed on their respective territories which guarantees fair and appropriate compensation to victims. The modalities of the national compensation schemes, however, remain the responsibility of the national authorities. Given that the scope of the EVZ differentiates from a national compensation scheme, the Commission is not in a position to assess its payments.
1 Council Directive 2004/80/EC of 29 April 2004 relating to compensation to crime victims, OJ L 261, 6.8.2004,
